name: Chicken 65
cuisine: South Indian (Chennai, Tamil Nadu; credited to Hotel Buhari, Mount Road, 1965; now a standard starter across India)

ingredients.name: Chicken thigh, boneless and skinless (or chicken breast)
Kashmiri red chilli powder (Kashmiri lal mirch)
Salt (namak)
ingredients.householdMeasure: a generous ¼ tsp (split between marinade and tempering)

ingredients.name: Curry leaves (kadi patta)
ingredients.householdMeasure: 1 sprig: 4–5 leaves chopped for the marinade + 10–12 whole leaves for tempering

ingredients.name: Oil (groundnut, sunflower or rice bran), for deep-frying
Green chilli (hari mirch)
ingredients.householdMeasure: 2 chillies, slit lengthwise (deseed for less heat)

ingredients.name: Dried red chilli (sukhi lal mirch), optional

equipment: Chopping board and a sharp knife (a separate board for raw chicken if you have one)
Mixing bowl (steel or glass) with a lid or plate to cover it while marinating
Small kadai (deep wok), about 18 cm across, for deep-frying
Plate lined with kitchen paper to drain
Small frying pan (tadka pan or a small non-stick pan) for the tempering
Clean kitchen towel to pat the curry leaves and chillies dry

No deep-frying (lower-oil alternatives): Air fryer: after coating, spray or brush the cubes with 1 tsp oil, spread them in one layer with gaps, and air-fry at 200°C for about 6–7 min, shake or turn, then 5–7 min more, until browned and the thickest piece is cooked through (75°C inside, or no pink and clear juices when cut)

steps.title: Rinse and dry the chicken
steps.text: Rinse 150 g boneless chicken briefly under cold water, then pat it completely dry with kitchen paper.
steps.tip: Wet chicken makes a soggy, patchy coating and makes the oil splutter.
steps.visualCue: The surface looks matt, not wet or shiny
steps.cameraCheck: The dried chicken on the board
steps.videoShot: Kitchen paper pressing down on the chicken and lifting away almost dry.

steps.title: Cut into cubes
steps.text: Cut the chicken into 2–2.5 cm cubes, about 12–14 pieces, trimming off any visible fat.
steps.tip: Wash the knife, board and your hands with soap after handling raw chicken.
steps.visualCue: Even, bite-sized pieces of similar size, so they cook at the same speed
steps.cameraCheck: The cubes spread on the board next to a spoon for scale
steps.videoShot: The knife slicing a strip of thigh into neat cubes.

steps.title: Chop the marinade curry leaves
steps.text: Pull 4–5 curry leaves off the sprig and chop them finely; keep the remaining 10–12 whole for the tempering.
steps.visualCue: Small green flecks on the board
steps.cameraCheck: The chopped leaves and the whole leaves in two separate piles
steps.videoShot: The knife rocking over a few curry leaves.

steps.title: Add the wet marinade
steps.text: Put the cubes in a bowl. Add 1 tbsp thick curd, 1 tsp ginger garlic paste and 1 tsp lemon juice.
steps.visualCue: White curd and paste sitting on top of the chicken
steps.cameraCheck: The bowl with all three added
steps.videoShot: The spoon of curd dropping onto the chicken cubes.

steps.title: Add the spices
steps.text: Add 1 tsp Kashmiri chilli powder, a pinch of turmeric, ¼ tsp garam masala, ¼ tsp cumin powder, ¼ tsp black pepper, the chopped curry leaves, and about two-thirds of the salt (a scant ¼ tsp).
steps.visualCue: Small heaps of red, yellow and brown powders on top of the curd
steps.cameraCheck: The bowl with the spices added, before mixing
steps.videoShot: Measuring spoons tipping the red chilli powder into the bowl.

steps.title: Mix well
steps.text: Mix with a spoon (or a gloved hand) for about 1 minute until every cube is evenly coated.
steps.visualCue: Every piece is evenly deep red-orange, with no white curd streaks
steps.cameraCheck: The mixed chicken in the bowl
steps.videoShot: A spoon turning the red-coated cubes over.

steps.title: Marinate
steps.text: Cover the bowl and leave it for 30 minutes at room temperature, or up to 24 hours in the fridge.
steps.tip: If it was in the fridge, take it out 15 minutes before frying so the cold chicken does not drop the oil temperature too much.
steps.visualCue: The marinade has clung to the chicken; little liquid left in the bowl
steps.cameraCheck: The covered bowl (or the bowl going into the fridge)
steps.videoShot: A plate being placed over the bowl.

steps.title: Dry the curry leaves and chillies
steps.text: Rinse the 10–12 whole curry leaves and 2 green chillies, then pat them completely dry with a towel.
steps.tip: Wet leaves in hot oil spit violently; dry them well.
steps.visualCue: No water droplets on the leaves
steps.cameraCheck: The dry leaves and chillies on the towel
steps.videoShot: The towel dabbing the leaves.

steps.title: Slit the green chillies
steps.text: Slit each chilli lengthwise; scrape out the seeds if you want it milder.
steps.visualCue: Chillies open like a book
steps.cameraCheck: The 2 slit chillies
steps.videoShot: The knife tip running down a chilli.

steps.title: Chop the garlic
steps.text: Peel and finely chop 2 cloves of garlic.
steps.visualCue: Small, even bits of garlic
steps.cameraCheck: The chopped garlic in a small heap
steps.videoShot: The knife chopping garlic into fine pieces.

steps.title: Add the flours
steps.text: Just before frying, sprinkle 1 tbsp cornflour and 1½ tsp rice flour over the marinated chicken.
steps.visualCue: White flour sitting on the red chicken
steps.cameraCheck: The bowl with the flours on top
steps.videoShot: The spoon of cornflour dusting over the chicken.

steps.title: Toss to coat
steps.text: Toss until the flour disappears and each piece has a thin, slightly tacky coating. If it looks wet and pasty, add 1 more tsp rice flour.
steps.tip: A thin, dry coat absorbs less oil than a thick, wet batter.
steps.visualCue: Pieces look fairly dry and evenly coated, not dripping
steps.cameraCheck: One coated piece held up on a spoon
steps.videoShot: A piece lifted from the bowl showing a dry, even coat.

steps.title: Heat the oil
steps.text: Pour about 250 ml oil into the small kadai and heat on medium-high to 170–175°C.
steps.visualCue: The oil shimmers; a pinch of the coating dropped in sizzles at once and rises within 2–3 seconds
steps.cameraCheck: The kadai with oil and the test pinch sizzling (or the thermometer reading)
steps.videoShot: The test pinch bubbling up to the surface.

steps.title: Fry the first batch
steps.text: Slide in half the cubes (6–7 pieces) one by one, with space between them.
steps.tip: Lower them in close to the oil surface to avoid splashes. Do not crowd the kadai; the oil cools and the coating turns soggy.
steps.visualCue: Lively bubbling around every piece
steps.cameraCheck: The kadai with the first batch
steps.videoShot: Pieces sliding into the oil off a spoon.

steps.title: Leave it alone, then turn
steps.text: Fry for 1 minute without touching, then turn the pieces with the slotted spoon. Keep the heat at medium-high.
steps.visualCue: The coating has set and does not stick to the spoon
steps.cameraCheck: The pieces being turned
steps.videoShot: The slotted spoon flipping a piece to show a set crust.

steps.title: Finish frying the first batch
steps.text: Fry 3–4 min more, turning once or twice, until deep reddish-brown and crisp.
steps.visualCue: Deep red-brown, crisp crust; the bubbling becomes quieter; a cut piece is white with no pink in the centre (75°C if you have a thermometer)
steps.cameraCheck: One piece cut open to show the cooked centre
steps.videoShot: A piece broken in half showing white, steaming meat.

steps.title: Drain
steps.text: Lift the pieces out with the slotted spoon, let the oil drip back for a few seconds, and put them on the kitchen-paper plate.
steps.visualCue: Pieces sitting on paper with little oil spreading under them
steps.cameraCheck: The drained first batch
steps.videoShot: The slotted spoon shaking over the kadai, then tipping the pieces onto the paper.

steps.title: Fry the second batch
steps.text: Let the oil come back to temperature (about 30 sec), then fry the rest of the cubes the same way, 4–5 min in total.
steps.visualCue: Same deep red-brown colour as the first batch
steps.cameraCheck: The second batch in the oil
steps.videoShot: The second batch bubbling.

steps.title: Drain the second batch
steps.text: Drain the second batch onto the paper with the first. Turn off the heat under the kadai.
steps.visualCue: All the chicken drained on paper
steps.cameraCheck: The full plate of fried chicken
steps.videoShot: A wide shot of the plate of fried pieces.

steps.title: Heat the tempering oil
steps.text: Heat 1 tsp oil in the small pan on medium heat (or use 1 tsp of the frying oil, pouring the rest out into a heatproof bowl).
steps.visualCue: The oil thins and shimmers
steps.cameraCheck: The pan with 1 tsp hot oil
steps.videoShot: Oil spreading across the hot pan.

steps.title: Fry the garlic
steps.text: Add the chopped garlic and stir for 20–30 seconds.
steps.tip: Do not let it go dark brown; it turns bitter.
steps.visualCue: Garlic turns pale gold and the raw smell turns nutty
steps.cameraCheck: The golden garlic in the pan
steps.videoShot: Garlic sizzling as the spoon stirs it.

steps.title: Add the chillies
steps.text: Add the slit green chillies and the dried red chilli (if using) and stir for 20 seconds.
steps.visualCue: Green chillies blister slightly and turn brighter
steps.cameraCheck: The pan with garlic and chillies
steps.videoShot: The chillies hitting the oil and blistering.

steps.title: Add the curry leaves
steps.text: Add the 10–12 dry curry leaves (stand back) and stir for 10–15 seconds.
steps.visualCue: Loud spluttering, then the leaves turn darker and crisp; strong curry-leaf aroma
steps.cameraCheck: The crisp leaves in the pan
steps.videoShot: Leaves crackling and curling as they hit the oil.

steps.title: Toss in the chicken
steps.text: Add all the fried chicken and the remaining salt (a pinch), and toss on medium-high for 30–60 seconds.
steps.visualCue: Every piece is glossy and dotted with garlic, chilli and curry leaves; no sauce in the pan
steps.cameraCheck: The tossed chicken in the pan
steps.videoShot: The pan being flipped so the chicken jumps and mixes with the leaves.

steps.title: Finish and serve
steps.text: Turn off the heat and squeeze a few drops of lemon over it (optional). Plate it with onion rings and a lemon wedge.
steps.tip: Eat it within 10 minutes; the crust softens as it sits.
steps.visualCue: Crisp, red pieces with dark-green fried curry leaves on top
steps.cameraCheck: The finished plate
steps.videoShot: A close-up of a piece being picked up, crust crackling, steam rising.

reasons: lean boneless chicken gives a lot of protein (about 32 g per serving) with little refined carbohydrate (about 13 g of flour coating) and no sugar, and the tempering adds garlic, curry leaves and chillies. Against that, it is deep-fried, about 36% of its calories come from added oil (about 25 g fat in total), sodium is moderate-high (about 850 mg), and it has almost no fibre or vegetables. Restaurant versions are usually bigger plates (about 200–250 g), often fried in oil reused through the day (which builds up oxidation products), may contain artificial red colour, and are often eaten with biryani or fried rice.

researchRating.basis: Chicken 65 is one of India's most popular chicken starters, a fixture on South Indian, Chinese-Indian and biryani-house menus nationwide. Swasthi's Recipes (indianhealthyrecipes.com) shows 5 from 340 votes, MyFoodStory 5 from 16 votes and Raksha's Kitchen 5 from 20 votes in search snippets; Swiggy's blog cites its own order analysis placing it as the most-ordered chicken item after chicken biryani (2017); and its origin story at Chennai's Hotel Buhari is widely retold (The Better India, Wikipedia). A version even appeared on MasterChef Australia. It is a little short of 5 because restaurant versions get mixed comments for being oily, artificially red or soggy, and because recipes and "authentic" claims are hotly disputed (egg or no egg, tempering or no tempering, bone-in or boneless).

storage: Fridge-safe for up to 2 days in an airtight box (refrigerate within 2 hours of cooking). Freezer: up to 1 month, but the crust will not fully recover. Reheat in an air fryer at 180°C for 4–5 min, or in a dry non-stick pan on medium heat for 4–5 min, tossing often, until piping hot in the centre. The microwave makes the coating soft and chewy. Raw marinated chicken (without the flours) keeps up to 24 hours in the fridge.
leftoverRemix: Chicken 65 kathi roll with mint mayo-curd. Reheat the leftover pieces in a hot pan until crisp, roughly chop them, and roll them in a warm roti or paratha with sliced onion, shredded cabbage, a squeeze of lemon and a spoon of curd mixed with mint chutney. It turns soft day-old pieces into a lunchbox roll where the crust does not matter.
burnOff: about 6.1 km of running (430 ÷ 70 kcal/km, for a 70 kg adult), or about 8.6 km of brisk walking (about 1 h 45 min at 5 km/h, using about 50 kcal/km for walking) (est.). The air-fried version (about 365 kcal, est.) is about 5.2 km running or 7.3 km walking.
